features.description: Outdoor Italy approach combining exploration, environmental storytelling, weapon combat, elemental route solving, optional Sound discovery, checkpointing, and direct entry into the Church Trial.
limitations: Procedural terrain, ruins, vegetation, props, and church architecture remain replacement-ready.
The playable footprint is compressed while implying a broader village region.
Current Goblin and Gremlin archetypes stand in for future location-specific enemies.

features.description: The integrated Church of Angels trial: exploration, elemental tests, combat rooms, Sound reveal, Animated Armor boss, reward, save flow, and exit.
limitations: Prototype geometry and procedural art remain replacement-ready.
Only the first Church Trial slice is integrated into progression.
Final animation, audio, cinematics, and balance are not represented.

features.description: Character-led authored quest using Tamsin dialogue, affinity-based relay repair, an illuminated signal trail, staged combat, physical evidence, quest journal stages, key-item rewards, persistent aftermath, and the reusable Authored Quest Framework.
limitations: Environment and character presentation remain procedural prototypes.
Goblin and Gremlin actors stand in for future location-specific enemies.
The eastern route opens but does not yet connect to a production region.

features.description: Complete character-led marsh quest combining Orin dialogue, resonance investigation, authored chapel and crypt environments, swimming traversal, a passive-to-hostile amphibious creature, three physical resolution routes, persistent aftermath, key-item rewards, and quest completion.
limitations: The chapel, crypt, Listener, lighting, and water presentation remain replacement-ready procedural prototype assets.
The Listener uses one encounter-specific authored behavior rather than a general creature-social AI framework.
Final animation, audio synthesis, voice acting, cinematics, and combat balance are not represented.
The opened marsh route does not yet connect to a production region.

features.description: Dedicated walkable benchmark for the reusable Weathered Cloister environment and prop kit, now including a contained stylized-PBR stone study, warm-key/cool-sky lighting calibration, layered architecture, shared weathered materials, water transitions, stairs, props, an operable iron gate, and global playability coverage.
limitations: The stylized-PBR treatment is provisional and intentionally limited to one calibration rock pending manual art-direction approval.
The first kit uses stylized primitive-based scene assemblies rather than imported production meshes or authored UV texture sets.
Only the Weathered Cloister material family and a compact architecture/prop vocabulary are represented in v1.
The water channel is a shallow decorative transition and does not replace the shared swimming-volume system.
Final decals, lightmaps, baked occlusion, destruction variants, and environment-specific art direction remain future asset work.

features.description: Permanent laboratory for elemental reactions, environmental element sources, Steam Burst pressure accumulation, and a mechanical lift that converts repeated chemistry into physical work.
limitations: Only five of sixteen core elements receive the refreshed visual pass.
Effects, sources, and machinery are procedural prototypes rather than final authored assets.
Pressure is a scalar resource and does not simulate gas temperature, volume, sealing, or pipe flow.
Laboratory targets and machinery prioritize deterministic systems testing over encounter design.

features.description: Shared physical substrate for material properties, vector fields, continuous force, torque, induced magnetization, polarity reversal, and material-specific magnetic response.
limitations: This slice proves field and material infrastructure rather than a complete circuit or electromagnetism engine.
Magnetic translation uses a stable gameplay approximation of field-gradient response.
Copper eddy currents, induction, circuit current, and charged-particle behavior are intentionally out of scope.
Geometry, materials, field visualization, and tuning remain replacement-ready.

features.description: A compact player-led puzzle combining Soul Grip, physical occlusion, mass-sensitive manipulation, a pressure switch, movable copper circuit topology, a motorized counterweight gate, and a breakable pickup reward.
limitations: The room uses procedural prototype geometry and explicit clue labels.
Soul Grip rotation is yaw-only in this version.
The copper fuse uses forgiving contact radii for controller placement.
Puzzle completion is not saved or connected to story progression.

features.description: First sustained concentration and weather prototype. Rain reserves 40 percent of maximum mana, makes Water spells free, supplies infinite atmospheric Water, wets authored outdoor targets, extinguishes exposed fire, and releases the full mana ceiling when dismissed.
limitations: Weather exposure is authored through the weather_exposed group; roof and interior occlusion are deferred.
Rain streaks are procedural prototype geometry rather than a final particle or screen-space renderer.
Rain, Snowfall, and Flight concentration are implemented; Thunderstorm, Smog, and Heatwave remain future effects.
Equipped ability costs are temporarily overridden and restored until a final spell-cost query layer exists.

features.description: All-unlocks combat and mastery laboratory for buffered Light and Heavy branches, context techniques, dash and aerial attacks, launch and juggle routes, stance breaks, critical strikes, defense, infusion, and exact temporary progression restoration.
limitations: Sword, Hammer, and Spear remain the primary authored production movesets; Chain and Whip have separate experimental laboratories.
Presentation is procedural and transform-driven rather than final skeletal animation.
Boss-specific break rules, executions, final animation, and balance remain deferred.

features.description: Second sustained weather prototype. Snowfall reserves 45 percent of maximum mana, makes Ice spells free, supplies infinite atmospheric Ice, accumulates across authored terrain, freezes exposed objects and water, weakens fire, and leaves temporary tracks.
limitations: Weather exposure is authored through the weather_exposed group; roof and interior occlusion are deferred.
Snow accumulation is a gameplay field rather than deformable terrain.
Slippery movement and load-bearing snow depth are deferred.
Equipped ability costs are temporarily overridden and restored until a final spell-cost query layer exists.

features.description: Shared aerial locomotion prototype spanning Double Jump, timed Hover, 75-percent Flight concentration, camera-relative six-direction movement, stable altitude braking, action restrictions, landing, and controlled descent.
limitations: Flight I permits movement only; aerial combat, ordinary casting, interaction, Soul Grip, and aerial Dodge are deferred to upgrades.
Hover duration and Flight reservation use fixed prototype tuning values.
Flight has no boost, dash, banking animation, speed tiers, or stamina interaction yet.
The chamber uses procedural geometry and visual route markers rather than scored checkpoints.

features.description: Composable three-dimensional airflow foundation using analytic vector fields, quadratic aerodynamic response, Gust, projectile deflection, traversal drift, updrafts, downdrafts, vortices, advected tracers and cloud particles, and a turbine consumer.
limitations: Analytic fields are gameplay vector functions rather than a full computational-fluid-dynamics pressure solver.
Solid geometry does not yet occlude or redirect airflow.
Drag uses gameplay scaling and acceleration caps for stable control.
Cloud particles are visual samples and the turbine is not yet connected to the circuit graph.

features.description: Shared constraint-based substrate for environmental rope, iron chain, chain and whip weapons, and Metal Tether traversal, proving sag, endpoint tension, momentum, overload failure, elemental material response, and counterweight load transfer.
limitations: Tether segments do not yet collide with level geometry or wrap around arbitrary obstacles.
The pulley uses a stable shared-length force model rather than wheel inertia or bearing friction.
Elemental reactions are direct laboratory inputs until production Fire and Ice payload receivers are connected.
Persistent actor binding, simultaneous multi-tethers, full free-ended whip propagation, and obstacle wrapping are intentionally deferred.

features.description: First flexible weapon class, combining authored orbit and slam intent with the shared iron-chain solver, swept weighted-tip contacts, momentum-scaled impact, and a seven-attack branching moveset.
limitations: The weighted tip uses authored hybrid trajectories and swept queries; the chain does not yet wrap around arbitrary level geometry.
Persistent latching, pulling, binding, and entanglement are deferred.
Elemental conduction through the combat chain is deferred.
Whips now use a separate tip-speed and wave layer over the same runtime-rig hook; chains remain weighted momentum weapons.

features.description: Distinct flexible weapon class using a shared leather tether, visible traveling-wave timing, swept tip-only contacts, speed-scaled sonic cracks, airflow deflection, and a material wrap-and-pull interaction.
limitations: The handle and tip use authored hybrid trajectories; the flexible body between them remains physically solved.
Wrap contact latches only for the current attack and does not yet persist as an actor-binding state.
The whip does not yet wrap around arbitrary level geometry or collide along every flexible segment.
Production elemental lash, burning, freezing, disarming, and item-retrieval behaviors are deferred.

features.description: Equippable Metal grapple spell with visible anchor acquisition, radial and tangential swing dynamics, reeling, momentum-preserving release, anchor overload, rigid-load transfer, airflow response, and a shared flexible conductive filament.
limitations: The tether constrains one player and one anchor; multiple simultaneous filaments are deferred.
The gameplay constraint is analytic CharacterBody locomotion while FlexibleTether3D provides the shared segmented material presentation.
The filament does not yet wrap around arbitrary level geometry.
Enemy binding, Lightning conduction, Flight integration, camera assistance, and accessibility auto-release are deferred.

features.description: Authored support-graph physics connecting sustained weight, redundant load paths, payload impacts, combustion weakening, cold brittleness, flexible-tether release, and Metal Tether extraction to visible structural collapse.
limitations: Connections are authored support edges rather than automatically generated finite-element meshes.
Supported members remain frozen until disconnected instead of flexing continuously.
Falling debris uses normal rigid-body collision but does not procedurally fracture into smaller persistent pieces.
Stress distribution uses member weight and active connection count rather than beam angle, torque, or cross-section.
Metal Tether extracts one authored brace at a time.

features.description: Compact objective encounter combining world-aware guards, optimized Smoke concealment, Gust, Firebolt, Metal Tether, Hammer impacts, authored structural collapse, debris hazards, reusable sound evidence, and a shared escape consequence.
limitations: Prototype geometry and procedural materials do not imply final foundry art direction.
Structural collapses use authored support graphs rather than automatic mesh decomposition.
Collapse damage is a radial gameplay consequence layered over physical debris collision.
Guards use perception and local movement without a navigation mesh.
Encounter completion is not saved or connected to story progression.

features.description: Safe runtime chamber for resource overcharge, Infinite Stamina and Mana, Focus slowdown comparison, stat inspection, and exact snapshot restoration.
limitations: Most non-resource stats remain Partial or Dormant by design.
The chamber is a development instrument, not a player allocation menu.
No leveling, equipment bonuses, respec, or permanent cheat state is included.

features.description: Linked spatial surfaces that transform relative position, orientation, CharacterBody and rigid-body momentum, angular velocity, and GenericProjectile trajectories through one reusable orthonormal mapping.
limitations: Portal interiors are emissive indicators rather than recursive rendered views.
Portals are authored whole surfaces and do not cut arbitrary openings into level meshes.
Characters remain upright because the current controller assumes world-up gravity.
Flexible tethers, gas volumes, navigation, and enemies do not cross portal boundaries in v1.
Objects teleport as a whole and cannot straddle both spaces.

features.description: Controlled four-lane comparison of the existing cautious, bold, skittish, and brute Goblin personality profiles against identical Poison Bloom hazards.
limitations: The room is an artificial tuning instrument rather than encounter design.
Enemy movement uses local steering rather than navigation-mesh pathfinding.
The smoke test verifies profile initialization; personality readability still requires manual comparison.

features.description: Frequency-selective Sound physics with energy accumulation, damping, sympathetic coupling, mechanism activation, fracture thresholds, and an adjustable Resonant Pulse spell using a dedicated ResonancePayload.
limitations: Frequency bands are gameplay-scaled rather than acoustic-material measurements.
Propagation is radial and does not yet model occlusion, reflection, diffraction, or room acoustics.
Natural frequencies are authored instead of derived from mesh geometry and material dimensions.
Sympathetic transfer is local energy coupling rather than a full wave equation.
Final audio synthesis, controller rumble, and production animation are deferred.

features.description: Two-round survival and reward loop connecting breakable supply containers, data-driven enemy loot, magnetic world drops, an unlocked three-choice reward chest, saved consumable inventory, visual Field Kit assignment, Healing Flask commitment, thrown Oil and Noise Makers, defense, stance breaks, and reset flow.
limitations: Guard uses a universal magical-metal surface rather than weapon-specific block animations.
Perfect Guard timing and defense costs are first-pass tuning values.
Bespoke hazards and bosses that bypass EnemyBrain still need to opt into the common defense resolver.
Production animation, audio, hit stop, controller rumble, and accessibility timing assists are deferred.
Healing Flask, Oil Flask, and Noise Maker are the first three authored quick items.
The survival-trial combat brains do not investigate Noise Maker stimuli; the Perception Laboratory remains the authoritative AI-response test.
Loot v1 uses authored weighted consumable tables; currencies, rarity tiers, equipment affixes, crafting materials, shops, and pity rules are deferred.
Reward chests expose three world-space supply choices; production chest cinematics and unique reward presentation are deferred.

features.description: Permanent gallery for procedural elemental presentation. The Water wing demonstrates generated surfaces, waterfall motion, impacts, wakes, churn, bubbles, electrical response, replay controls, and reserved bays for all sixteen core elements.
limitations: Only the Water wing is populated in v1.
Advanced reflection, shoreline response, underwater camera treatment, and ocean rendering are deferred.
The room is a development gallery rather than a story location.

features.description: Dedicated launch, juggle, fall, slam, landing, and recovery presentation space for light, medium, and heavy airborne targets using the shared weapon and reaction pipeline.
limitations: Presentation uses procedural transforms rather than final skeletal animation.
The laboratory isolates target reactions and is not an authored encounter.
Boss-specific airborne resistance and final balance remain deferred.

features.description: Dedicated Ice laboratory for temperature-driven freeze fronts, seeded crystal growth, arbitrary-plane frost, stress-driven cracking and shattering, thaw presentation, and procedural Ice Lance visuals.
limitations: Frozen-water collision, skating friction, and load-bearing thickness are deferred.
Shards are presentation particles rather than persistent rigid bodies.
Arbitrary world objects require an authored FreezeState component before they can freeze or fracture.

features.description: Persistent shared-player campus connecting combat and mastery, aerial reactions, movement, interaction, status, and ability-range stations with fast travel, reset, temporary unlocks, and exact progression restoration.
limitations: The hub intentionally does not contain every repository capability.
Dedicated laboratories remain authoritative for detailed tuning.
Campus geometry and fixtures are developer presentation rather than final world art.

features.description: General-purpose playground for interactables, receivers, surfaces, enemy waves, developer vision, audits, and rapid scenario experiments.
limitations: The sandbox is intentionally eclectic rather than a designed encounter.
Objects may represent older and newer prototype generations side by side.
Sandbox state is disposable and is not a progression contract.

features.description: Five-segment outdoor expedition from cypress basin through wet woodland and longleaf ridge toward foothills and Blue Ridge forest, with authored early segments, route familiarity, optional discovery, checkpoints, shared regional state, and four live animals using reusable water, climbing, and burrowing habitats.
limitations: Only Cypress Basin, Wet Woodland, and Pine Ridge have authored layout passes.
Rocky Foothill Camp and Blue Ridge forest remain prototype route segments.
Regional presentation and traversal assets remain replacement-ready.
The four field animals prove authored Mob Engine integration; their procedural bodies, habitat placement, and ambient population are prototype presentation rather than final regional ecology.

features.description: Regional route-selection and persistence prototype connecting mapped destinations, expedition entry, route familiarity, segment state, and return flow.
limitations: The map represents a prototype regional network rather than final geography.
Combined map and route-familiarity persistence previously required focused validation.
Only the current Wilds route is developed beyond placeholder destination data.

features.description: Playable Mob Engine laboratory comparing data-driven movesets, personality, drives, intentions, effects, vitals, perception, relationships, bonding, persistence, and shared ground/swimming/flight/climbing/burrowing locomotion across eight live animals and three reusable habitat types.
limitations: Procedural animal silhouettes and movement are prototype presentation rather than final models or animation.
The shared pond, climb wall, burrow route, and procedural animals provide focused locomotion tests rather than finished exploration ecology or final encounter spaces.
The climb proof covers one vertical surface; ceiling/corner transitions and full body orientation remain future authored traversal work.
The burrow proof uses visible translucent soil; finished terrain occlusion, entrances, exits, and deformation remain authored presentation work.
Generic contact effects use active-phase reach rather than animation-authored hit volumes; projectile effects reuse the established GenericProjectile.
Pack, herd, predator/prey, summon, and faction ownership remain actor-provider policy.

features.description: Named-animal field course for injury, rescue, healing, feeding, persistent bonding, navigation-aware following, authoritative companion commands, dynamic rebaking, stuck detection, and separation recovery.
limitations: The rescue course is an artificial validation space rather than an authored world encounter.
Runtime navigation baking and conservative separation recovery are prototype-safe, not final large-world streaming solutions.
Moving-obstacle avoidance and authored traversal links remain deferred.

features.description: Registry-driven controller-first launcher and health dashboard for permanent development scenes and their validation contracts.
limitations: This is a developer launcher, not a production level-select menu.
It does not inspect open pull requests or resolve branch conflicts.
It reports registry and local resource health, not creative quality.
